# SIGN TEST (two-sided exact binomial, H0 p=0.5)
# turbo q15 alone : n=64  wins=47 (0.73) median +0.425  p=2.3e-04
# THE CONTROLLED TEST. Only ZENSR_DATA differs. The 24k arm is a SUBSET sliced
# from the 100k set (tools/make_data_subset.py), so both arms share generation
# process, teacher, target dtype (f16), crop size and the IDENTICAL val tail.
# Same box (so same bf16), same init (none, from scratch), same 120k steps,
# batch 48, lr 3e-4, qboost 3, same seeds. No warm restart.
# RESULT: 4x the training data helps ONLY at the lowest quality. Significant at
# q15 (p=2.3e-04 for turbo, median +0.425 — near the 0.3 resolution threshold,
# so this one is plausibly a real difference rather than only a direction),
# fading by q35, and indistinguishable from zero at q55 and above.
# This RESOLVES the two earlier confounded attempts: both averaged over the
# whole q range, where a q15-only effect washes out to nothing. Their "null"
# was not wrong so much as the wrong question.
# Training-metric check, again: the big arm's val_psnr_vs_teacher was 38.42 vs
# the small arm's 38.19 across ALL q. That gap predicted neither the size nor
# the location of the real effect.
